title: Orbital-selective oxygen holes in cuprate ladders beyond the Zhang-Rice paradigm
authors: Chengyun Hua, Tianran Chen, Isaac C. Ownby, Colin L. Sarkis, Garrett Granoth, Masaaki Matsuda, Jiaqiang Yan, Ho Nyung Lee, Jeongkeun Song, Yuya Shinohara, Masatomo Uehara, Jun Akimitsu, Oleksandr Prokhnenko, Eugen Weschke, Takeshi Egami, D. Alan Tennant
abstract: The electronic structure of the spin-ladder cuprate Sr14Cu24O41 challenges the presumed universality of the Zhang-Rice singlet (ZRS) framework and models based exclusively on Cu-O hybridized orbitals. Combining polarization-dependent resonant soft X-ray scattering at the O K-edge with inelastic neutron scattering, we show that doped holes in the Cu2O3 ladders localize predominantly in planar non-bonding O 2pz (pπ) orbitals of rung oxygen sites rather than forming conventional ZRS states. Polarization-resolved RSXS uniquely identifies this orbital assignment, while lattice and magnetic excitations reveal its coupled consequences, establishing a unified microscopic picture that excludes the conventional σ-bonded singlet. This oxygen-sublattice charge order produces an anomalous diagonal stretching phonon and explains the absence of incommensurate magnetic fluctuations and anomalous magnon splitting. These findings motivate a reassessment of hole pairing in ladder cuprates and the sufficiency of copper-centric models for cuprate superconductors.
summary: This paper uses advanced X-ray and neutron scattering techniques to investigate hole localization in cuprate ladders. It demonstrates that holes reside primarily in non-bonding oxygen $p\pi$ orbitals rather than forming standard Zhang-Rice singlets. This orbital selectivity suggests that the electronic structure requires models beyond simple copper-centric descriptions for understanding superconductivity.
main_problem: The study challenges the conventional Zhang-Rice singlet (ZRS) framework by investigating the orbital character of doped holes in cuprate spin ladders.
main_result: Doped holes localize predominantly in planar, non-bonding O 2pz ($	ext{p}\pi$) orbitals on rung oxygen sites, which is distinct from conventional $\sigma$-bonded singlet states.
method: The research combines polarization-dependent resonant soft X-ray scattering (RSXS) with inelastic neutron scattering (INS) measurements to probe orbital and lattice excitations simultaneously.
model_or_system: The physical system is the spin-ladder cuprate $	ext{Sr}_{14}	ext{Cu}_{24}	ext{O}_{41}$. The analysis compares experimental findings against theoretical models, noting that conventional three-band Hubbard models are insufficient.
key_observables: Orbital character of holes (via RSXS polarization dependence), anomalous diagonal stretching phonon (from INS), and the energy/intensity of specific X-ray resonances ($	ext{O}$ K-edge).
important_parameters: The doping level, temperature evolution of charge order, and the orbital symmetry ($p\pi$ vs $\sigma$-bonded) are key parameters.
main_assumptions: The necessity of a multi-probe approach (RSXS + INS) is highlighted because single techniques provide only limited projections of the complex electronic state.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the structure, polarization dependence of charge order reflections at the O K-edge, and temperature evolution of resonant intensities, alongside INS data showing anomalous phonon modes.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by identifying the limitations of existing models (ZRS), presenting multi-technique evidence (RSXS/INS) to pinpoint the orbital localization ($	ext{O}(2)$ $p\pi$), and concluding with a unified picture that requires reassessing hole pairing mechanisms.
why_interesting: The work provides crucial experimental constraints on strongly correlated electron models, particularly by identifying an orbital degree of freedom (the $\pi$-band) that is decoupled from the primary magnetic exchange pathways, which is vital for understanding high-Tc superconductivity physics.
